name: Fernandez-Vargas v. Gonzales
summary: The Court upheld application of a new immigration statute to a noncitizen who had re-entered illegally, illustrating the wide deference courts give Congress in structuring immigration law and its retroactive application.
significance: The government cites this case for the proposition that Congress has broad authority to restructure the rules governing immigration judicial review and that courts must respect the statutory framework Congress creates.
